title: Normalized derived augmentation square for finite cosimplicial totals
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and use ordinary derived categories, localization $Q$, and the K-injective right derived functor $RF$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $\Delta$ have the finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]$ and order-preserving maps as its objects and arrows. For a strict functor $C:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}^{\ge0}(\mathcal A)$, put $T(C)^r=\bigoplus_{n+q=r}C_n^q$ and $d_T=\delta+(-1)^n d_C$, where $\delta=\sum_i(-1)^i C(d^i)$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Let $A,B$ be nonnegative complexes, let $b:\operatorname{const}(A)\to K$ and $c:\operatorname{const}(B)\to J$ be strict augmentations, and let $v:A\to B$ and $u:K\to J$ be quasi-isomorphisms (columnwise for $u$) with $B,J_n$ termwise injective and $u_nb_n=c_nv$ for every $n$. The maps $a:A\to T(K)$ and $a_J:B\to T(J)$, equal to $b_0$ and $c_0$ in cosimplicial degree zero and zero in higher cosimplicial degrees, are chain maps and satisfy $a_Jv=T(u)a$. With $\beta_J:F(T(J))\cong T(FJ)$ the finite-biproduct comparison, $\rho_E:RF(QE)\cong QF(E)$ the inverse derived unit, $c_v=\rho_B RF(Qv)$, and $\chi_u=Q\beta_J\rho_{T(J)}RF(QT(u))$, one has
$$\chi_u RF(Qa)=Q(\beta_JF(a_J))c_v.$$
The chain map $\beta_JF(a_J)$ has component $F(c_0)$ in cosimplicial degree zero and zero elsewhere. Under the column comparisons $\rho_{J_n}RF(Qu_n)$ and $c_v$, its source maps correspond to $RF(Qb_n)$. If $(h,f)$ is a strict map between two augmented diagrams, so $f_nb_n=b'_nh$, any compatible strict lifts $(\widetilde h,g)$ with $g_nc_n=c'_n\widetilde h$ satisfy the total augmentation square; after localization the displayed equation commutes with that square. These statements hold for every such compatible choice of augmented nonnegative injective replacements [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

proof.text: Write $\iota_{n,q}$ for the diagonal inclusions. The augmentation identities for the two maps $[0]\to[1]$ give $K(d^0)b_0=b_1=K(d^1)b_0$. Hence $\delta b_0=(K(d^0)-K(d^1))b_0=0$. Since $b_0$ is a chain map and the vertical sign at $n=0$ is $+1$, the total differential satisfies $d_T\iota_{0,q}b_0^q=\iota_{0,q+1}b_0^{q+1}d_A$. Thus $a^q=\iota_{0,q}b_0^q$ is a chain map. Replacing $(A,K,b)$ by $(B,J,c)$ proves the same for $a_J$. In degree $q$, $a_Jv$ and $T(u)a$ are respectively $\iota_{0,q}c_0^qv^q$ and $\iota_{0,q}u_0^qb_0^q$; the assumed augmentation square makes them equal. These calculations use the signed total of [def-sp-double-complex-total].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-injective-finite-total-derived-comparison] to $u:K\to J$. Its hypotheses hold because every $J_n$ is nonnegative and termwise injective and each $u_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. It supplies the summand-preserving $\beta_J$, the quasi-isomorphism $T(u)$, and K-injectivity of $T(J)$ and $J_n$. Apply the same statement to the constant cosimplicial diagram on $B$ and its identity replacement: its column $B$ is K-injective as well. By [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], the natural derived unit $\eta_E:QF(E)\to RF(QE)$ is invertible on these complexes; put $\rho_E=\eta_E^{-1}$. Since $v$ and $T(u)$ are quasi-isomorphisms, $c_v$ and $\chi_u$ are precisely the isomorphisms specified in the statement.

Naturality of the unit in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], applied to $a_J:B\to T(J)$, says $RF(Qa_J)\eta_B=\eta_{T(J)}QF(a_J)$. Multiply by the two inverse components to obtain $\rho_{T(J)}RF(Qa_J)=QF(a_J)\rho_B$. Using step 1 and functoriality, compute
$$\begin{aligned}\chi_u RF(Qa)&=Q\beta_J\rho_{T(J)}RF(Q(T(u)a))\\&=Q\beta_J\rho_{T(J)}RF(Q(a_Jv))\\&=Q\beta_J QF(a_J)\rho_B RF(Qv)\\&=Q(\beta_JF(a_J))c_v.\end{aligned}$$
This is equality in $D(\mathcal B)$ of the entire derived-object maps, not just equality on cohomology.

proof.text:
By the defining summand identity for $\beta_J$ in [lem-sfb-injective-finite-total-derived-comparison], $\beta_J^qF(\iota_{0,q}c_0^q)=\iota'_{0,q}F(c_0^q)$. Thus $m=\beta_JF(a_J)$ has precisely the asserted degree-zero cosimplicial component and all other components zero. For every $n$, naturality of the unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] at $c_n:B\to J_n$ gives $QF(c_n)\rho_B=\rho_{J_n}RF(Qc_n)$. Therefore
$$QF(c_n)c_v=\rho_{J_n}RF(Q(c_nv))=\rho_{J_n}RF(Q(u_nb_n))=c_{u_n}RF(Qb_n),$$
which is the asserted correspondence of the augmentation maps under the specified column and source comparisons.

source.place: Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), summand-preserving finite-total equality, and Tags 070Y/070K, natural derived unit.

proof.text:
For a second augmented diagram use primes. A strict augmented map satisfies $f_nb_n=b'_nh$; a compatible strict lift satisfies $gu=u'f$, $\widetilde h v=v'h$, and $g_nc_n=c'_n\widetilde h$. Degree-zero components give $T(f)a=a'h$ and $T(g)a_J=a'_J\widetilde h$, while every higher cosimplicial component of these composites is zero. The natural finite-total comparison of [lem-sfb-injective-finite-total-derived-comparison] gives
$$T(Fg)m=T(Fg)\beta_JF(a_J)=\beta_{J'}F(T(g)a_J)=m'F(\widetilde h).$$
This is the strict total augmentation square, including its mapped version.

source.place: Tag 0141 (lemma-functorial-injective-resolutions and remark-match), strict augmented squares, and Tag 015J (lemma-two-ss-complex-functor), finite-total equality; direct component calculation.

proof.text:
Naturality of the unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] at $\widetilde h$ and $T(g)$ gives
$$QF(\widetilde h)c_v=c_{v'}RF(Qh),\qquad QT(Fg)\chi_u=\chi_{u'}RF(QT(f)).$$
For the first equality expand $c_v$, use $QF(\widetilde h)\rho_B=\rho_{B'}RF(Q\widetilde h)$, and substitute $\widetilde h v=v'h$. For the second, expand $\chi_u$, use $T(Fg)\beta_J=\beta_{J'}F(T(g))$ from [lem-sfb-injective-finite-total-derived-comparison], then $QF(T(g))\rho_{T(J)}=\rho_{T(J')}RF(QT(g))$, and substitute $T(g)T(u)=T(u')T(f)$. Combining these equalities with steps 3 and 5 yields
$$QT(Fg)\chi_u RF(Qa)=Qm'c_{v'}RF(Qh)=\chi_{u'}RF(Qa')RF(Qh).$$
Thus the displayed derived equation commutes with the localized augmented square. Every calculation used only the stated compatibility equations and injectivity assumptions, so it holds for every compatible choice of replacements and lifts.
